title: Dad has never camped. So why does his stew taste exactly like Grandad's?
premise: On a high moor beside an old stone fire ring with three seats, Dad takes Grandad's place for the autumn camp and knows far too much for a man who has never camped, while someone in heather purple with hands as big as the tent door stands one stepping stone nearer the fire each night.
twist: Dad has been ringing Grandad every evening from the bottom of the hill to be talked through the camp, and the stew is Grandad's recipe from the dented flask, so the thing that seemed like a replacement was a call for help.
world: A high autumn moor in heather and peat with black bog pools, a ring of old grey stones, a moss-green ridge tent, a drystone wall and a field gate down the hill.
